newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP, SEASON-ENDING AWARDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP, SEASON-ENDING AWARDS.

text.p: Although the outcome was delayed a day, it was never in doubt, as Tom Lehman cruised to victory Monday in the $3 million Tour Championship and claimed some prestigious season-ending awards.
Lehman, who began the final round at Southern Hills with a nine-stroke lead, shot a one-over-par 71 to finish at 12-under 268, six strokes ahead of Brad Faxon, who posted a 68.
"I was extremely nervous starting today, I don't know why," said British Open champion Lehman. "When you have a big lead it's over, in everyone's mind at least, but there are no gimmes in golf.
"That's why I wanted to play, it was important to deal with that pressure and the negative thoughts, rather than just having it handed to you. I wanted to earn it."

Lehman earned $540,000 for winning the Tour Championship, giving him a PGA Tour record $1,780,159 in season winnings. He also clinched the Vardon Trophy for best scoring average, and PGA Player of the Year honours.

Said Lehman, "the money title is nice, but I've never put a lot of emphasis on money. I've always been more impressed by the guys who win the Vardon Trophy or are Player of the Year, those are better indicators of who had a good year."

Rain washed out Sunday's play, and most weeks that would have reduced an event to 54 holes, but the PGA Tour decided the season-ender was important enough to warrant playing the final round on Monday. The last events to play a full round on Monday were the 1988 British Open and the 1983 Masters.
Lehman started and ended his round badly, bogeying two of the first three holes as well as two of the last three. Four mid-round birdies ensured that those bogeys really did not matter.

"Yesterday was a very tough day for me, just waiting around and thinking more about the round. As a result, I came out today a bit unsure of myself," said Lehman, who was also runner-up at this year's U.S. Open.

"I don't know why it's so difficult to play with a huge lead, but it's tough to come out of the first tee with the right attitude. Making two bogeys at the start may have been a blessing because it got me mad and I started playing better."
Faxon began the round in a tie for second with Vijay Singh of Fiji, who shot a 74 and finished ninth.

"I had mixed emotions about playing because I really didn't have much to gain," Faxon said. "It's harder to play for second, to play just for money rather than trying to win, but Tom basically ruined everyone's chances to win."
Faxon sank a two-foot putt for par at the 18th to finish solo second ahead of Steve Stricker (65) and cross the $1 million mark in season earnings.
"It's the biggest money of my career," said Faxon. "I kept thinking that this is a million dollar putt, though of course it actually wasn't."
Faxon ended up at $1,055,050, one of nine million-plus earners for the 1996 season.
